elements.contents:
Sugar-rich foods exacerbate antibiotic-induced microbiome disruption

Avoiding a diet rich in simple sugars during treatment with antibiotics may mitigate microbiota disruption.

  • Anqi Dai
  • Annamaria Ballweg
  • Jonathan U. Peled
ArticleOpen Access30 Sept 2026

elements.title: Type 2 immune history trains lung macrophages for viral disease tolerance (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Type 2 immune history trains lung macrophages for viral disease tolerance

Type 2 inflammation trains nerve- and airway-associated macrophages to confer disease tolerance against lethal influenza by limiting immunopathology and promoting tissue repair without enhancing viral clearance.

  • Payal Damani-Yokota
  • Yavor Yordanov
  • Kamal M. Khanna
ArticleOpen Access30 Sept 2026

elements.title: Global mangrove distribution on the open coast is controlled by waves (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Global mangrove distribution on the open coast is controlled by waves

A process-driven mangrove presence or absence model using 20 years of open-source wave data shows that wave conditions are critical in determining where mangroves grow worldwide.

  • Sarah Wells
  • Bradley Henderson
  • William Glamore
ArticleOpen Access30 Sept 2026

elements.title: X-ray liquidography decodes complex motions in azobenzene isomerization (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
X-ray liquidography decodes complex motions in azobenzene isomerization

Time-resolved X-ray liquidography films the structural changes of azobenzene during trans-to-cis isomerization in solution with atomic-level precision.

  • Jungmin Kim
  • Hosung Ki
  • Hyotcherl Ihee
ArticleOpen Access30 Sept 2026

elements.title: Histone readers MLLT1 and MLLT3 concentrate AID to confer locus specificity (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Histone readers MLLT1 and MLLT3 concentrate AID to confer locus specificity

By being restricted to target regions by MLLT1–MLLT3 occupancy, activation-induced deaminase activity is able to avoid most off-target mutagenesis during B cell somatic hypermutation.

  • Noé Seija
  • Sophia Gannon
  • Javier M. Di Noia
Article30 Sept 2026

elements.title: Carbene transfer from thianthrenium ylides for cyclopropanation (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Carbene transfer from thianthrenium ylides for cyclopropanation

Thianthrenium ylides can be used as a general platform for metal–carbene generation and transfer, including cyclopropanation, σ-bond insertion and sigmatropic rearrangements.

  • Deepak Behera
  • Sagnik Chatterjee
  • Tobias Ritter
ArticleOpen Access30 Sept 2026

elements.title: An amygdala to anterior hypothalamic circuit gates stress sensitivity (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
An amygdala to anterior hypothalamic circuit gates stress sensitivity

The anterior hypothalamic nucleus regulates negative valence in the brain, highlighting a new pathway that controls sensitivity to stressful events and signposting approaches to identify new circuit interactions relevant to mental health.

  • Zachary T. Pennington
  • Alexa R. LaBanca
  • Denise J. Cai
ArticleOpen Access30 Sept 2026

elements.title: Dynamic protrusions mediate crawling motility in Asgard archaea (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Dynamic protrusions mediate crawling motility in Asgard archaea

Anoxic live-cell imaging shows actin-dependent crawling motility and dynamic protrusions in Asgard archaea, providing insights into cellular innovations that may have contributed to eukaryotic evolution.

  • Philipp Radler
  • Tobias Viehboeck
  • Christa Schleper
ArticleOpen Access30 Sept 2026

elements.title: Osteoclasts intercept meningeal lymphatic paths for dural metastasis (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Osteoclasts intercept meningeal lymphatic paths for dural metastasis

Osteoclast-derived angiopoietin-2 in the dura mater impairs lymphatic vessel function and weakens anti-tumour immunity against dural metastases, which offers new therapeutic approaches to restore meningeal lymphatic function through selective osteoclast targeting.

  • Rui Zeng
  • Jiaxu Zhao
  • Yudan Chi
Article30 Sept 2026

elements.title: Population-scale immune multiome atlas reveals regulatory disease mechanisms (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Population-scale immune multiome atlas reveals regulatory disease mechanisms

Population-scale simultaneous profiling of chromatin accessibility and gene expression across immune cells reveals regulatory architectures that connect genetic variants to disease.

  • Masahiro Kanai
  • Toni M. Delorey
  • Meri Lähteenmäki
Article30 Sept 2026

elements.title: Human genetics implicates a BACH2–NRF2 axis in fetal haemoglobin activation (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Human genetics implicates a BACH2–NRF2 axis in fetal haemoglobin activation

BACH2 restrains activation of the fetal-haemoglobin-encoding γ-globin genes, while loss of BACH2 enhances NRF2 chromatin occupancy and promotes the formation of activation foci at the γ-globin genes.

  • Chun-Jie Guo
  • Uma P. Arora
  • Vijay G. Sankaran
ArticleOpen Access30 Sept 2026

elements.title: Prion-like transmission of human tau strains in the mouse brain (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Prion-like transmission of human tau strains in the mouse brain

Mouse experiments show that Alzheimer’s disease and corticobasal degeneration tau filaments retain their distinct structures during templated seeding, supporting strain-specific tau propagation and disease modelling.

  • Sofia Lövestam
  • Aki Shimozawa
  • Sjors H. W. Scheres
ArticleOpen Access30 Sept 2026

elements.title: Wafer-scale epitaxy growth of high-mobility p-type boron carbon nitride (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Wafer-scale epitaxy growth of high-mobility p-type boron carbon nitride

A dual-precursor chemical system is used to achieve wafer-scale epitaxy growth of boron carbon nitride, a high-performance p-type semiconductor, for potential integration in efficient 2D materials for electronics.

  • Chien-Chih Tseng
  • Chang-Hsun Huang
  • Vincent Tung
Article30 Sept 2026

elements.title: Transcription pause and elongation regulators mediate somatic hypermutation (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Transcription pause and elongation regulators mediate somatic hypermutation

The molecular factors and mechanisms that mediate the chromatin recruitment of activation-induced deaminase and the generation of its stalled polymerase II substrate during somatic hypermutation are identified.

  • Lizhen Wu
  • Anurupa Devi Yadavalli
  • David G. Schatz
ArticleOpen Access30 Sept 2026

elements.title: GPCR antagonism via rewiring of receptor trafficking and degradation (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
GPCR antagonism via rewiring of receptor trafficking and degradation

A strategy for functional G-protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) antagonism through bispecific antibody-mediated endocytosis and lysosomal degradation is reported.

  • Kaitlin Rhee
  • Lawrence Shue
  • Xin Zhou
ArticleOpen Access30 Sept 2026

elements.title: γδ T cell receptor dependencies define a unique immunosurveillance modality (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
γδ T cell receptor dependencies define a unique immunosurveillance modality

Tissue-resident γδ T cells mount rapid, innate-like stress responses that require γδ T cell receptor signalling, revealing lineage-specific receptor dependence that underpins their conserved roles in immunosurveillance and informs therapeutic deployment.

  • Nicolas Veland
  • Bethania Garcia-Cassani
  • Miguel Muñoz-Ruiz
ArticleOpen Access30 Sept 2026

elements.title: Spatiotemporal clonal architecture of the newborn mouse forebrain (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Spatiotemporal clonal architecture of the newborn mouse forebrain

Clonal barcoding across the newborn mouse forebrain reveals developmental principles whereby glutamatergic neurons and astrocytes remain locally derived, whereas widely dispersed GABAergic (γ-aminobutyric acid-producing) lineages link neurons with oligodendrocyte precursor cells.

  • Guohua Yuan
  • Michael Kunst
  • Tomasz J. Nowakowski
Article30 Sept 2026

elements.title: Scalable decision-making for games of imperfect information (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Scalable decision-making for games of imperfect information

Ataraxos, an AI for the board wargame Stratego, establishes a design pattern for reinforcement learning and search that is effective under large amounts of hidden information, a longstanding desideratum of the field of strategic decision-making.

  • Samuel Sokota
  • Eugene Vinitsky
  • Gabriele Farina
ArticleOpen Access30 Sept 2026

elements.title: Evolution of terrestrial anatomy revealed by a derived stem tetrapod (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Evolution of terrestrial anatomy revealed by a derived stem tetrapod

New anatomical evidence reclassifies Westlothiana as an aquatic stem tetrapod, showing that terrestrial limb adaptations evolved mosaically in transitional amphibious environments before crown tetrapods emerged.

  • Ben Igielman
  • Xavier Jenkins
  • Roger Benson
Article30 Sept 2026

elements.title: Butterfly wing patterns in flight create powerful illusory motion cues (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Butterfly wing patterns in flight create powerful illusory motion cues

Butterfly wing patterns and flight dynamics work in tandem to create powerful visual illusions that confuse predators, potentially representing one of the most successful visual defence strategies in moving animals.

  • George R. A. Hancock
  • Emmanuelle S. Briolat
  • Jolyon Troscianko
ArticleOpen Access30 Sept 2026
